strategy.summary: The Orders API spec added POST /orders/{id}/cancel (cancelOrder) and changed GET /orders/{id} (getOrder): `totalCents` became a required `total` Money object {amount, currency}, and `status` may now be `cancelled`. The existing getOrder test asserts the old shape; it must assert `total` instead (keeping every other check), and new cases must cover cancelOrder's 200/404/409 responses and a cancelled order read back through getOrder.
inScope: test/orders.test.js: update the getOrder 200 assertion from totalCents to total, nothing else in it
New cases in test/orders.test.js for cancelOrder (200, 404, 409) and getOrder returning status cancelled, with a cancelOrder request helper beside the existing placeOrder one
assumptions: Tests run in-process against the real app (createApp on port 0), as the existing suite does; nothing is faked.
The store always prices orders in USD (src/store.js), so the expected total for 2 Kettles is {amount: 4998, currency: 'USD'}.
Each test places its own order and uses only the id that call returned; the 404 cases use an id (999) no test can reach with the suite's few orders, as the existing getOrder 404 test does.

risks.description: Clients reading totalCents break silently if the test still asserts the old shape
risks.mitigation: TC1 asserts the exact new body with toEqual, so a reintroduced totalCents or missing total fails.

risks.description: Cancelling twice could succeed or change state again
risks.mitigation: TC5 asserts 409 with the Error shape on a second cancel.

acceptanceCriteria.text: GET /orders/{id} 200 returns {id, productId, quantity, status, total} with total a Money object {amount (integer, cents), currency (USD|EUR)} and no totalCents
GET /orders/{id} returns status 'cancelled' for an order that was cancelled
POST /orders/{id}/cancel on a placed order returns 200 with the Order, status 'cancelled'
POST /orders/{id}/cancel on an unknown id returns 404 with an Error body {error: string}
POST /orders/{id}/cancel on an already cancelled order returns 409 with an Error body {error: string}

testCases.title: returns an order with its total
preconditions: App listening on a random port
steps: Place an order for product 1, quantity 2
testCases.expected: 200, application/json, body equals {id, productId: 1, quantity: 2, status: 'placed', total: {amount: 4998, currency: 'USD'}}
testCases.rationale: getOrder (GET /orders/{id}) at test/orders.test.js:48 asserted totalCents, which the spec removed in favour of required total Money.

testCases.title: returns a cancelled order with status cancelled
steps: Place an order for product 3, quantity 1
testCases.expected: 200, body equals the order with status 'cancelled' and total {amount: 699, currency: 'USD'}
testCases.rationale: getOrder's status enum now allows 'cancelled', which a caller sees after cancelling.

testCases.title: cancels a placed order
steps: Place an order for product 3, quantity 2
testCases.expected: 200, application/json, body equals {id, productId: 3, quantity: 2, status: 'cancelled', total: {amount: 1398, currency: 'USD'}}
testCases.rationale: New operation cancelOrder (POST /orders/{id}/cancel): its success response.

testCases.title: is 404 when cancelling an unknown order
is 409 when cancelling an order already cancelled
steps: Place an order for product 3, quantity 1
testCases.rationale: cancelOrder's documented 409 response for an already cancelled order.

strategy.environmentNotes: No external services: the suite starts the app in-process with createApp() on an OS-chosen port, as test/orders.test.js already does.

cases.title: POST /orders refuses a quantity under one
POST /orders is 404 for an unknown product
POST /orders is 409 when the stock is short
GET /orders/{id} returns an order with its total
GET /orders/{id} returns a cancelled order with status cancelled
GET /orders/{id} is 404 for an unknown order
POST /orders/{id}/cancel is 404 when cancelling an unknown order
POST /orders/{id}/cancel is 409 when cancelling an order already cancelled
